text: Despite many gamers being socially
awkward individuals, RPGs never truly
let us roleplay that type of character.
It's always expected that you'll
converse with the local idiots to
complete their quests, purchase items,
or even just gather your allies. But
what if you were so shy and introverted
that the idea of speaking with another
person was worse than the choice of
death? Can you beat Balders's Gate 3
without talking to others? We begin this
journey as Shadow Heart for reasons
which will be revealed later. And
immediately upon loading into the game,
Shadow Heart speaks. Where am I?
Clearly, we're going to need some ground
rules for this run. It will only count
as talking if anyone in my party speaks
to someone else. Talking to yourself is
okay. Spell casting is fine. And because
Larry uses a different style text for
non-vocal options in their cutscenes,
it's easy to see what you can and cannot
select. Unfortunately, these rules only
save me for about 20 more seconds
because Lazelle jumps down to be the
first roadblock of the challenge. Any
option you can select here immediately
fails the run. You don't get many tools
this early into the game to get by here.
So, my first idea of tactically playing
with the prism to ignore her totally
failed. The next idea was using the
minor illusion high elf racial to lure
the imps over and start combat. This two
doesn't work. However, it increases your
vision range, letting you spy on the
imps like a filthy perve. With them in
your sights, you can issue an attack
command on them, and your character will
do it in the background during the cut
scene with Lzelle. Starting combat
before I need to speak. I double checked
in the dialogue history screen to ensure
that no words are spoken, something I
will be doing frequently. And so that
our socially awkward hero and Lzelle
never risk speaking with one another, I
stripped the superior Gthani armor from
her back before forcing Lazelle to jump
to a certain doom. With her gone,
there's no danger of further social
interaction throughout the rest of the
Nautaloid. The battles are won, the
transponder transponded, and the beach
begins. However, something very unusual
happened when I regain control of my
character this time. Lzelle normally
leaves her party as soon as the
Nautaloid is complete. But an unexpected
bonus of the minor illusion dialogue
skip I'd found is that Lzelle remains in
your party, not needing to be recruited.
I wasn't sure how to handle this yet, as
I can't exactly ask her to wait in camp.
That would be cheating. So, I decided to
leave her dead for now, ignoring her
like all the other many problems in my
life. After all, it's not like any other
companion can be recruited without a
word on my behalf. From here, I set off
to participate in the goblin gate
battle. It went as smoothly as ever, but
entering the grove is far too risky with
Zevllor there waiting an ambush to offer
friendship. The usual YouTuber method of
dialogue skipping to level four ain't an
option today. So I targeted the weakest
enemies in the region before sneaking
below the blighted village to feather
fall into the underdark. This got me to
level three and I multiclass to the new
cleric of stars druid subclass. Unlike
other playthroughs, any class choice I
make is permanent as withers cannot be
spoken with to change it later. The
starry druid subclass has a lot of solid
early game solo power. For example, it's
dragon breath I used to kill steal this
minotaur is a high damage bonus action
attack that can't miss. something we all
know Shadow Heart needs desperately. I
also figured animal form to be a pretty
good tool to prevent myself from
speaking. The XP down here is nice, but
the real reason I beline for the
Selunite outpost is the luminous armor.
When dealing radiant damage, this armor
reduces enemy attack roles, synergizing
overpoweredly with the star druid's
radiant attacks. It's so broken that
early game battles where you're
completely outnumbered become a walk in
the park, even while going full shadow
horde and missing threequarters of your
attacks. As a cat, I set Barkcus free.
He gave no thanks, just as I'd hoped. In
the blighted village, I got ready to
face off solo against several level four
ogres. Using dash and star archer
arrows, I was able to kite the creatures
all the way to the grove. Spider form
got me inside because this cowardly
teling refused to open the gate. And I
used this combat status to make my way
past all these normally chatty
individuals just to gather a bit of
minuscule XP from feeding a fish to a
bear. This also got me into Kaga's room
where I had the brilliant idea to
destroy the necromancy of Thay. It did
work, but not really in the way I
expected. Arabella suddenly died without
cause. Kaga rightfully claimed I
betrayed her and a war broke out within
the grove. Once these shadow creatures
fell, the other druids left me alone
with Kaga. Big mistake. I haven't lost a
1v one since my days on Rust. She got
owned. I'd only just began this
challenge and my refusal to speak and
attempts to be clever already ended up
getting a lot of innocent people killed.
And while I'd normally be bothered by
all these failed future quests, this
time I couldn't care less. To continue
my streak of instigating wars, I'd
figured I'd try luring the Kithani over
to Walkin's rest. I read a comment from
a viewer that claims that this causes
them to fight one another. But as we all
know, 90% of the advice given out on
YouTube are lies and [ __ ] Could
this be the mythical 10%. Turns out yes.
I happily watched as these flaming fists
absolutely deleted my githani stalkers.
Wasn't even close. They may be too
incompetent to open a door, but they
easily handled the toughest outdoor
encounter of act one. To show my thanks,
I freed Floric as a badger, evading her
quest rewards entirely and continued
fighting nles around the region using my
starry hit-and- run tactics. For a
change of pace and a break for murder, I
met up with Scratch. The animal handling
options here allow you to recruit the
pup without uttering a word. Dogs truly
are the perfect companion for any
socially inept adventurer. My animal
forms let me explore the world without
fear of communication from humankind
everywhere except for the goblin camp,
of course. That's because once you
trigger the handsome Goreach cutscene,
and yeah, that's its name. Now, you'll
lose the ability to long rest within the
region because a certain dream visitor
will appear and force you to speak. In
my book, it doesn't matter if it's a
dream, that's still speaking and it's
illegal. Because of that, I saved the
goblin camp for last and headed straight
for Grim Forge. But after defeating the
Dwagar with some gusts of wind, I
learned that upon arrival, you're forced
into a conversation without any attack
options available, despite the fact that
this lady dwarf is clearly threatening
me. What gives, Lyen? My saving grace
came in the form of a deadly zel.
Because she's still in the party, I
could swap to her during the cut scene
and then select a summoned creature.
Using it to instigate the fight before
Shadow Heart needs to speak. Murder Hobo
and Grim Forge more than made up for all
that missed quest XP that you'd normally
find in act one. And it's like they
always say, if you can't help him, you
may as well kill him. As a decked out
level five, I crossed the bridge to
trigger the handsome Gortes cut scene,
slaughtered all the goblins without a
long rest, and returned to Lace L. You
can't lift glowy magical light bulbs, so
she's revived and killed again so her
corpse could accompany me to the
mountain pass. No life nerds at home
like myself probably realize this should
be the end of the challenge. Entering
the mountain pass forces a long rest and
in your camp you need to speak with
Raphael before you can continue. There
are exploits to let you knock out
Raphael and long rest anyways. But even
then, your dream visitor scene plays
out, forcing you to talk there,
accepting reality has never been
something I was good at. So rather than
call it quits now, I set out in search
of a brand new skip. It's like that
Minecraft meme about finding diamonds.
Never give up on your dreams, kids. Time
to throw random [ __ ] at the wall and see
what sticks. Maybe a spectator in my bed
could break my dream. Of course not.
That's stupid. Could I go through Grim
Forge instead? Again, doesn't work. 45
minutes of further nonsense ensued until
I discovered this rather simple trick.
Place the mysterious artifact into your
hot bar for easy access and then leave
the region. After clicking yes to the
prompt asking if you want to continue to
the mountain pass, spam the hotkey that
your artifact is on. The game then tries
to pull up the cutscene, but because
you're already in a cutscene, it doesn't
know what to do. You then immediately
long rest, ignoring your dream visitor
and wake up in camp during the day with
Raphael standing in the corner like a
chump. Because it's daytime, you can
just leave your camp, moving you
directly to the mountain pass, skipping
all of those supposed act one mandatory
dialogues, verified, of course, by
opening my dialogue history. At least
I'll somehow managed to self-revive only
to be killed again. And it's off to the
crush to exterminate the rest of her
people. Since I'm forced to be
multiclassed as a level one cleric the
entire game, I figured I'd use the most
broken brain deadad combo in existence
to make my life easier. Despite being
almost a 2-year-old game at this point,
Moon Beam can be cast without
interrupting the immunity granted by
Sanctuary. I don't know why. Larry and
has patched much stupider things than
this. And yet, you can still cast Moon
Beam to delete nearly anything in the
game without them fighting back. It's
great XP here. And lore wise, we all
know how Shadow Hart feels about Gith.
The only section which took some finesse
was to skip Blackest dialogue. By
maintaining the combat status with the
Gith Yankee soldiers and just solving
the statue puzzle whilst in combat, you
can ignore her and claim the blood of
Lethander. With that, it came time to
enter the shadow curse lands.
Immediately upon loading into act two,
Lazelle again self-revived and decided
she'd talk without being told to do so.
Can you feel it? Not okay. I reloaded
and thought maybe the Grim Forge path
would work, but doing so again causes
Lazelle to speak to me. I'd thought you
insufferable. I went back to option one,
and funny enough, the solution this
time, as with most things in life, is
violence. Use the attack option as
quickly as possible upon loading into
act two, and Lazelle doesn't have time
to say a word. To be doubly sure she
asked TFUs, I turned Lazelle into a
bear. Bears can't talk no matter how
many children's books lie and say that
they can. Plus, it's about time we
changed up the left side portrait on the
screen. This seemingly pointless
decision ended up saving me moments
later, as I'd probably have lost the
battle against the goblin caravan up the
road if not for Bezel. While act one
wasn't really all that bad, as I could
just spam long rest as much as I wanted,
for the rest of the game, I could never
long rest again, or else that dastardly
dream visitor will appear and force me
to speak. No vendors means potions are
hard to get. So efficiency is going to
be the key. As luring my enemies seems
to be working quite well, I figured I'd
try leading the Dryer all the way to
Last Light in. I crossed the bridge,
stepping in, hoping the Harpers would
take my side. But upon arrival, they
rage war upon me. Much like YouTube did
when I demonetized my corpse explosion
only video. Like come on, how was I
supposed to know that weaponizing
corpses isn't familyfriendly? Clearly
outnumbered, I sanctuary and hoped for
the best. Thankfully, they all ignored
my unargetable ass to kill Carnis,
including Fist Marcus. Strangely enough,
he ended up doing most of the work,
letting me scoop up the Moon Lantern at
the cost of just one spell slot. After
escaping combat into the prison, I used
my cat form to inconspicuously steal the
Harper's valuables, then attempted to
equip the Moon Lantern on Lazelle. A bit
of a mistake because that pixie
immediately locked her into a dialogue,
which couldn't end without a word. Yet
again, Shadow Cat was forced to slay her
own ally. Poor Lazelle, you really chose
the wrong leader this time. I dragged
the Moon Lantern the same way a cat
would do it, to reach Moonrise Towers,
unharmed by the curse. Additional perks
of being a cat are that you're not
expected to speak to the guards upon
arrival. They ignored my approach,
allowing me to reach the tower's summit.
Up here, I used minor illusion to lure
skeletal minions to the safety railing
free edge and toss them off one by one.
With the undead dead, I snuck into
Belleazar's room, bailing seven rolls in
a row to get inside for a less talkative
moon lantern. From there, my list of
moonrise tasks is complete, and it was
back into the shadow curse, straight
over Raphael's head, and into the
gauntlet of Char. Basar's goon saw right
through my insect disguise with a unique
voice line to boot. Luckily, I didn't
have to speak, nor did I have to fight
as I fled, leaving those bone boys to
die. The easiest trial was, of course,
completed. I know this maze like the
back of my ass at this point. An
umbrelled now was the spear of night.
It's just next door. I stealthy obtained
the book, then snuck back in as a cat.
Because they're small enough to jump
directly through the bars of this door.
The spear is mine, all without pissing
off any of Char's warriors. Mainly cuz I
didn't want to do the other trials, I
snuck into the Mason's Guild to get the
only knock scroll you can find in act
two. Invisibly, I sidestepped Char's
warriors, placed the gym, and was jump
scared by Lady Char. Being a god, she
has the power to lock Shadow Heart into
a conversation, and the run was dead if
not for Lazelle. She used the
triedand-true murder method to get me
out of talking with my own god, revived
me, and saved the day. We knocked our
way into the Shadowfell, and as I
clicked into there, another Shadow Heart
cut scene played. Sweat ran down my brow
as I prayed she wouldn't speak. She
didn't. Now within Char's domain, Bazar
appeared to speak to me. Thankfully,
Larry let us avoid that one with a
non-vocal option. I then lured him to
the cliff's edge and pushed him to his
death. Now, the entire reason I'd picked
Shadow Heart was for exactly this
moment. There is no way to kill or avoid
speaking with the Night song unless you
were Shadow Heart. She alone has the
kill option and kill she did do.
Panthers and I exited the Shadowfell to
be surprised by a rhyming devil. For a
brief moment, my heart sunk until I saw
that beautiful attack option sitting in
the corner. It just straight up ends the
scene. Another bullet dodged. I returned
back to Moonrise for the rooftop Cathric
encounter. And once again, those
anti-introvert socialist devs at Larian
Studios force you to talk. And this
time, there is no non-vocal option
available. No attack options either.
Additionally, any humanoid on this
rooftop is forced to join the
conversation, and the game even shifts
you out of animal forms to do it.
Another speed bump in the road that is
the life of proxy. Dozens of minutes of
experiments took place, leading to a new
solution. This time, Scratch is the
hero. Although had I known about this
earlier, I would have definitely planned
a stronger summon than Scratch because
any summon is able to be here on the
rooftop without joining the
conversation, id expected I could use
one to attack Katherine and start the
battle. But oddly enough, that doesn't
work. Instead, Katherrick and his dog
totally ignore anyone hitting them for
more than 20 minutes. Scratch
continuously bit Kather's ass,
absolutely chewing it apart. The
absurdity of a dude just sitting here
waiting for 20 minutes for Shadow Hart
to reply to what he said in the
conversation while a dog continuously
bit his ass had me laughing. I dropped
him below 50% health, but nothing was
really changing. What did work to break
the conversation was to kill Shadow
Heart, and I'd once again avoided what
Larry probably thought is an undgeable
cut scene. Thanks to the best boy our
party narrowly maneuvered the rooftop
Katherric encounter to enter the mind
flare colony. A muchneeded pseudo long
rest was used, and I farmed the local
populace to reach level 8. Down the
elevator we went, one big bear and a
shadow heart. Colony Katherrick is a bit
of a weird part of this otherwise
totally normal challenge run because you
can absolutely kill him without any
dialogue just so long as you stay wild
shaped from start to finish. But the
strategy I'm using today is my tower to
heaven. While I hate using the same
Merkel strategy two videos in a row,
there is a reason I need to do this.
You'll see soon. My tower of crates was
built and because of how high up I am,
Shadow Heart is outside of range of the
combat trigger. From this height,
throwing objects will deal 50 plus
damage per hit, guaranteeing Kather's
loss. Before looting the Nether Stone
from the freshlymade corpse, Shadow
Heart continued building her tower
higher until being so high that this
happens. Do you see it? After reaching a
certain height, the map is no longer
red. You can now waypoint out of here
and run directly to the end of act two.
Before doing so, Lazelle loots the
Nether Stone as an owl bear to avoid the
Dream Visitor confrontation, and she
moves to join Shadow Heart. The whole
reason for that tower escape route is
because when your main character uses
the portal to escape, you're normally
ambushed by your dream visitor and
forced to speak to them when exiting
Moonrise Towers, something we definitely
can't have happen. Upon loading into the
Act 2.5 campsite, Lizo, understandably
pissed off by my poor leadership,
attempts to ruin the day by insulting
me. But thankfully, this too is
dodgeable by reloading and spamming the
artifact to snub her once more. Don't
celebrate too soon, though, because as
soon as you long rest, you're going to
be ending up in another dialogue.
There's no switching delay. The artifact
dodges don't work and the game even
despawns your summons so they can't kill
you in your sleep. Pretty weird that
Larry thought of that. I tried a bunch
of random stuff until throwing a
spectator at Lazelle the exact moment I
went to sleep freed Lzelle from the cut
scene. There's no question in my mind as
to why Lazelle hates me so much. Because
she's in combat, she didn't get to sleep
and she used invisibility to flee the
encounter. Shadow Heart is then murdered
in her sleep by her companion to avoid
speaking. The Gthani instantly appeared
and into the portal we went. Approaching
the emperor again, it prompts me to
talk, avoidable by spam clicking a
summon minion to bunk shadow heart at
top her head. That's about the 20th time
now that Larry's tried to force me to
speak. And after a struggle of an
encounter where I just barely came out
the victor, the emperor immediately
locks me down once more and has his way
with me. I went back to my oh so many
strategies which have got me out of
talking in the past. Self bonking didn't
work. Wild shapes proved ineffective.
And the emperor even stripped me of the
oh so precious astral prism. I was
completely stumped. I went back and did
some testing on another save file and
did discover a way to skip it using
silent shenanigans. However, doing so
completely screws you as the emperor
will only open up the exit portal after
you've talked with him. Skipping this
dialogue will soft lock your game. It's
official. On patch 8, you cannot beat
Balders's Gate 3 without speaking to
others. All because of one narcissistic
mind flare. But I still have unanswered
questions. How many words must be said?
How many people must be spoken with? And
is the rest of the game completable?
Yeah, of course the initial challenge
has failed. But I know none of you want
to watch me give up mid nonsensical
nightmare. I fully explored this
dialogue tree, mapping it out to
perfectly speak as little as possible.
All in all, this chatty mother mind
flare forced 30 words out of us. And it
was off to camp. Spectator bro watched
over us in our sleep. The leave camp
option got me away without a fight. And
now in act three, it's time to head into
the city to face more problems. To avoid
speaking with an orphan child, I broke
my own ankles and disguised myself as a
cat to sneak into the keep. I paused to
observe Gortash's coronation from
multiple angles and eventually made my
way into the lower city. Just like act
two, long-resting is banned because of
the emperor being a social butterfly.
But unlike act two, we have another
option. Helsa gave up her life without a
fight. Really not sure as to why, but
thanks to her, the elves are accessible.
I avoided hope by killing Shadow Heart
again, not accepting the disguise she
offers. Instead, I snuck in to steal my
own from a nearby wardrobe. This
clothing lets you walk around here
undetected. And in Raphael's bedroom are
the restoration faucets. On tactician
difficulty, it's an unlimited amount of
long rests. Just so long as you don't
piss off Raphael, you can keep coming
and going as you please. As shopping
isn't allowed, I raided Leroin's place
for supplies, locking into both a
strength elixir and a globe of
invulnerability scroll. I then
continuously robbed his illusionary
shopkeep blind. The shopkeep isn't a
real person, so you can pickpocketed an
unlimited amount of times without anyone
caring, even if you fail. Just be sure
to be hidden in a cloud of fog. Orin's
Nether Stone is our first target. To get
to her, you got to deal with the local
murderer named Dolan. I think that's his
name. Anyways, I forget and I'm too lazy
to go look it up now. He was dealt with
and his password secured. The problem
with passwords, though, is that they're
words. And for all I know, there's some
dude on the other side of the door
waiting to hear me speak the word and
then opening the door. I'm much too
socially enough to take that risk.
There's got to be a better way. Into the
sewers we went. The artifact snub trick
let me ignore a fake Orin to dodge her
little chat. Then I could panther buy a
manslaughter chasm to reach Orin's door.
Historically, boxes have solved a lot of
my problems in past challenge runs. And
if there's two things I learned this
day, it's number one, don't use a torch
in this area. And number two, the Ball
Temple is one of the rare fully box
proof fortresses within this world.
Thankfully, I had seen a technique used
by Bouch where you stuff a bunch of
chests up against the door and spam jump
into it to clip through. I can confirm
on patch 8 it still works without flaw.
Orin, who remains in Yenna form with 5
HP, is then knocked out. The ballless
nether stone is cleaned, and no one
nearby seemed to mind, oddly enough. I'd
never seen anyone escape the area
without speaking, but I figured why not
try the chests again. And to my
surprise, it worked. Together, we left
the region for Worms Rock Fortress.
Catzel walted into the back of the room
and used her Yankee Mage Hand to drink a

trigger cutscene, so it was able to
return to the throne room and kidnap
Gortach straight from his ceremony,
bringing him back to our camp. I know
it's much easier to just throw him off a
cliff, but I read a comment the other
day complaining that I never fight
Gortach. So, here you go. Gortach failed
to defend himself in a seven verse one
situation. And secretly, I'd hoped that

block the cut scene you get when you go

This cutscene makes zero sense.
Gortach's corpse is nowhere near the
key. And worst of all, that damn emperor
forces you to talk again. Thankfully,
the game auto saves as soon as Gortach

swapped to my elemental bow right before

than talk to that squidface gaslighter.
So, die I did do. Kind of amazing how
often that trick works to avoid a
conversation. Back in the lower city,
the Elder Brain tasked us with killing
Orin, but thankfully didn't ask me for
my input. Before going any further, I
rob Vologre of his fireworks and

celebrations. Good guy Raphael let us

Liselle clearly didn't join my boat

off. And the emperor pulled me into the

And with that, we've replaced our Gith
